cultural.vision_reason: A painted wooden marionette dressed in Burmese court attire with acheik-style textile pattern, sequins, and metal-thread embroidery—a classic Bamar traditional puppet ('mintha' figure). This is clearly Burmese-made costume and craft.

physical.title: puppet
physical.summary: Painted wooden marionette of a Burmese prince, or 'mintha'. The figure is dressed in court attire and wears a textile in the 'acheik' (wave) design distinctive of the Mandalay court. However, these figures post-date that period by a short time. The court attire is interwoven with metal thread and embellished with streams of sequins. The lower garment is dark red. The upper is green and white. The facial features are carefully painted, including the folds of skin on the neck. The puppet's hair may well be horse hair. The figure is attached to a wooden handling frame by cotton threads, with which it would have been manipulated. The figure is one of a pair: 2005.0618.1 & 2.
